nodes.characterization_summary: No significant morphology change for commercial WO₃ and WO₃-1.2 GPa; abundant bulk holes/defects visible in WO₃-H₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2 presents the high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) images of commercial WO₃, as well as samples prepared by thermal annealing... abundant holes traversing the bulk structure were visible in WO₃-H₂

properties.description: Large white particle with small white inclusion (50 nm scale bar)

nodes.characterization_summary: Periodic [WO₆] octahedra resolved in WO₃-1.2 GPa; OVs visible as missing O atoms on surface but ordered structure in bulk.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure 2d, WO₃-1.2 GPa was further analyzed by an integrated differential phase contrast (iDPC)-STEM image. The periodic atomic columns of W and O were clearly resolved... OVs were distinctly visible as points of 'missing' atoms... on the surface

properties.description: Rectangular lattice structure with dots (2 nm scale bar)

nodes.characterization_summary: No evident change in crystal structure for WO₃-1.2 GPa and WO₃-H₂; decreased XRD peak intensities attributed to presence of OVs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure S4, the X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns confirmed that no evident change in the crystal structure was observed for WO₃-1.2 GPa and WO₃-H₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: Distinct symmetrical peak at g=2.002 from unpaired electrons trapped by OVs; peak intensity of WO₃-1.2 GPa significantly stronger than WO₃-H₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure S6, the presence of abundant OVs in WO₃-1.2 GPa and WO₃-H₂ was confirmed by the emergence of a distinct symmetrical peak at g = 2.002...

nodes.characterization_summary: WO₃-1.2 GPa and WO₃-H₂ exhibit enhanced absorption in visible region (450-800 nm) due to new discrete energy bands from OVs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure S7 displayed the UV–vis diffuse reflection spectroscopy (UV–vis DRS) spectra. Compared to the pristine WO₃, WO₃-1.2 GPa and WO₃-H₂ exhibited enhanced absorption...

nodes.characterization_summary: UV Raman (surface-sensitive): broader/less intense peaks and fwhm=57.9 cm⁻¹ at 767 cm⁻¹ for WO₃-1.2 GPa indicate high surface OV concentration; visible Raman: fwhm=18.2 cm⁻¹ at 796 cm⁻¹ comparable to WO₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure 3a,b, UV and visible Raman spectra... were collected to study the spatial distribution of OVs. The UV Raman spectra are more sensitive to the surface region... fwhm of the main Raman shifts at 767 cm⁻¹ was fitted to be 57.9 cm⁻¹ for WO₃-1.2GPa... In the visible Raman spectra... fwhm of the main Raman peak at 796 cm⁻¹... was 18.2 cm⁻¹ for WO₃-1.2GPa

properties.description: WO3 with H2 (likely hydrated or hydrogenated form)

nodes.characterization_summary: fwhm of main peak at 796 cm⁻¹ is 18.2 cm⁻¹ for WO₃-1.2 GPa (comparable to 17.4 cm⁻¹ for WO₃) vs 24.0 cm⁻¹ for WO₃-H₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the visible Raman spectra (Figure 3b and Table S1), the fwhm of the main Raman peak at 796 cm⁻¹... was 18.2 cm⁻¹ for WO₃-1.2GPa...

Plot of relative energy (eV) vs Bulk-Surface
Oxygen atoms originally from tungsten trioxide

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s: peaks at 530.5 eV (lattice) and 531.7 eV (OVs); more evident 531.7 eV peak and positive BE shift for WO₃-1.2 GPa surface; no bulk shift after Ar plasma etching (~50 nm removal).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure 3c, the spatial confinement of OVs on the surface of WO₃-1.2 GPa was further demonstrated by the X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). The peaks around 530.5 and 531.7 eV were assigned to the lattice oxygen and oxygen species chemisorbed at surface OVs... To obtain information from the bulk region, the samples were treated with argon plasma etching, which removed approximately 50 nm from the surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: Exciton binding energy Eb=44.2 meV for WO₃-1.2 GPa vs 55.9 meV for pristine WO₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure 4a, the exciton binding energy (Eb) estimated by the temperature-dependent photoluminescence (PL) spectra... was found to be 44.2 meV for WO₃-1.2 GPa...

nodes.characterization_summary: Slopes for WO₃-1.2 GPa and WO₃-H₂ much smaller than pristine WO₃, indicating increased carrier density.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure 4b, the slopes fitted for WO₃-1.2 GPa and WO₃-H₂ were much smaller than that of pristine WO₃, indicating that OVs can increase the carrier density...

nodes.characterization_summary: WO₃-1.2 GPa shows reduced radius in Nyquist plots due to surface OVs improving charge transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure S14, the generation of OVs led to a reduced radius in Nyquist plots of the electrochemical impedance spectrum (EIS), and WO₃-1.2 GPa delivered a much smaller radius...

nodes.characterization_summary: Notable enhancement in photocurrent for WO₃-1.2 GPa and WO₃-H₂ under 420 nm LED.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure 4c, a notable enhancement in photocurrent was observed for WO₃-1.2 GPa and WO₃-H₂...

nodes.characterization_summary: No hydrogen intercalation detected in WO₃-H₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure S5, the solid-state ¹H NMR spectra indicated that no hydrogen intercalation occurred in WO₃-H₂.
